<a id="add-revision-cloud"></a>

### Add revision cloud

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-14 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** draw a revision cloud around these elements on this view.

Draws a revision cloud around a set of elements in one view, tagged to a revision the project already has. **It belongs to the revision, not to the drawing.** A cloud carries a revision id, and that id is what puts the change on the revision schedule in the titleblock. A cloud on a view with no revision behind it is a shape on a drawing that no register mentions - which is the failure mode this job has when it is done by hand in a hurry. **The revision comes from the request, and is not invented.** Picking "the latest revision" automatically is wrong often enough to matter: the newest revision in the sequence is frequently the one being prepared for next time, and clouding this week's change onto it issues nothing.

The field's own name says which kind<br>**padding mm** - a number - digits only - 250 or 250.5, not 250mm |
| **You get** | created |

**How to use it**

1. Open the model in Revit and connect Heron: press **Heron** on the Heron tab, so its heron turns orange.
2. Select what it works on in Revit (elements) - or name it in the same request, and Heron finds it first.
3. Turn **Changes** on in Heron's **Settings** (Heron tab).
4. In a Claude chat, ask in your own words, for example *"put a revision cloud around this"*. Say the values under **You say** in the same sentence.
5. Heron makes the change as **one entry in Revit's Undo list**. With **Ask to Keep** on, Revit asks **Keep or Discard** first; Ctrl+Z takes it back.

<a id="center-viewports-on-sheets"></a>

### Center viewports on sheets

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-02 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** a viewport sits off-centre on its sheet - move it to the middle of the title block.

Moves the one viewport on each sheet so that its box sits in the centre of the sheet's title block, and says where each one was and where it went, in millimetres on the paper. **THE TARGET IS THE CENTRE OF THE TITLE BLOCK'S EXTENTS ON THE SHEET** - the whole title block, title strip included, which is the paper. A sheet's own outline is not the paper. **MEASURED BEFORE IT MOVES, READ BACK AFTER.** A viewport already within half a millimetre of the centre is named in `alreadyCentred` and not touched, so a second run moves nothing - which is also the read-back. A move counts in `centred` only when Revit reads the new centre back at the target. A move that does not read back is PUT BACK where it was and named in `refused`, never left moved under a refusal; if even that cannot be read back, the run stops and nothing on any sheet is kept. **THE BOX IS WHAT IS CENTRED, AND THE BOX IS NOT ONLY THE PLAN.** A viewport's box takes in the view's annotation - elevation markers, tags, a visible crop region - so a marker out to one side pulls the drawing off the centre by half its distance. Nothing is hidden or cropped to make up for it. The box's size is reported beside the title block's, so a lopsided box shows in the answer rather than on the print. **SKIPPED AND NAMED, NEVER GUESSED.** A sheet with two viewports is `ambiguous` - which one is the plan is not answerable here. A sheet with no title block, or with two, has no single paper to centre on. A sheet with no viewport has nothing to centre. Each is named in its own list and nothing on it moves. **VERSION 2 CAN LINE THE SHEETS UP TO A MASTER instead** - the plan in the same place on every sheet, so it does not jump as the set is paged through. Name the master sheet and each viewport goes to the master's viewport centre. A sheet at another scale is skipped and named, and so is one whose title block sits at another origin: the centre is measured on the sheet, not the paper, and its title block is never moved. Version 1's proof no longer describes the code and is kept as a record; the card is DRAFT until it is proved again. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16), so a drawing set is one undo entry.

### Check sheet sets by parameter

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-13 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** which View/Sheet Sets are out of step with the sheet parameter value they are named for.

Answers, for one sheet parameter, which View/Sheet Sets are out of step with it - the sheets that carry a value and are not in the set named for that value, the sheets and views in that set that no longer carry it, and the values that have no set at all. A set is named for a value as the value itself, or with a prefix put in front. A question, read and never changed; it opens no transaction. **A PARAMETER NO SHEET HAS IS REFUSED, NAMING IT.** Empty and duplicate sets are LIST_SHEET_SETS' answer, not this one's.

<a id="create-revision"></a>

### Create revision

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-18 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** add a new revision to the project's revision schedule.

Creates a revision in the project and fills in its description, date, issued by, issued to, show (cloud and tag, tag or none) and numbering sequence - every column Add fills in Sheet Issues/Revisions. An empty value leaves Revit's default; the word <blank> writes an empty one. **It is the input ADD_REVISION_CLOUD could not get.** That fragment needs a `revisionId` and deliberately refuses to invent one - picking "the latest" automatically is wrong often enough to matter. Nothing in the library could produce one, so the whole revision job stopped at the first step. **A new revision is NOT issued unless `issueState` says `issue`.** Issuing locks the description, date, issued to, issued by and numbering, and no new cloud can go on it - right for recording an issue that has already gone out, wrong by default. It is never implied by another value, and it is set last. **Everything is checked before anything is made, and every column is read back.** A value that does not read back after the revision exists throws, and the add-in rolls the whole call back - never a half-filled row.

<a id="create-revision-numbering-sequence"></a>

### Create revision numbering sequence

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-23 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** make a new revision numbering sequence, numeric or alphanumeric, or duplicate one.

Makes a new revision numbering sequence - New and Duplicate in Sheet Issues/Revisions > Customize Numbering. Numeric takes minimum digits, a starting number, prefix and suffix; alphanumeric takes its custom sequence of values, prefix and suffix. With `copyFrom` it duplicates a sequence, keeping its type and every setting not given here. **THE TYPE IS FIXED ONCE MADE**, so a value belonging to the other type is refused by name rather than dropped. **CHECKED BEFORE IT IS MADE, READ BACK AFTER**: the name must be new and free of the characters Revit forbids, and Revit must call the settings valid. A sequence that does not read back as asked is rolled back. Empty leaves Revit's default or the copied value; <blank> writes an empty prefix or suffix. Revit 2022 on - earlier releases have no named sequences. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="create-revisions-from-sheet-dates"></a>

### Create revisions from sheet dates

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-18 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** create revisions for every date typed on the sheets.

Makes one revision for each distinct date typed in a text note on a sheet, and adds it to every sheet where that date is typed - one call, one Undo. A revision already holding that date and the same description is reused, never made twice. Only text typed on the sheet itself is read, exactly as FIND_DATES_IN_VIEWS reads it with sheetsOnly; a numeric month is refused. **ADDED, NEVER REPLACED.** A sheet keeps every revision it already lists. **REFUSED WITH NOTHING CHANGED** when no date is typed on a sheet, when the description is empty, or when two revisions already stand for one date. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="create-sheets"></a>

### Create sheets

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-24 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** add new sheets to the drawing register.

Creates sheets with the numbers and names given, on a chosen title block. **A SHEET NUMBER MUST BE UNIQUE AND REVIT ENFORCES IT AFTER THE SHEET EXISTS.** `ViewSheet.Create` makes the sheet with a number Revit picks; setting the wanted number is a second step that can be refused. So a clash leaves a **real sheet in the register under the wrong number** - and a count reports the job as done. This is the same shape as `DUPLICATE_SHEETS`, where the fragment being re-authored reported *"Duplicated 0 of 1"* while the sheet count went 2 to 3. **SO THE NUMBER IS CHECKED BEFORE ANYTHING IS CREATED.** A number already in the register is reported in `numberTaken` and no sheet is made for it. That removes the failure rather than cleaning up after it, and it means a re-run of the same job creates nothing instead of a second set of misnumbered sheets. **THE TITLE BLOCK IS A REQUEST INPUT WITH NO DEFAULT.** Revit will happily create a sheet with no title block at all, and a drawing register full of blank-bordered sheets is discovered at issue. Which title block a project uses is a project decision, not something this fragment may guess. **IT READS BACK BOTH THE NUMBER AND THE NAME**, because they fail independently: the number can be refused for a clash while the name is accepted, and the result looks correct in a list that shows only one of them. **IT DOES NOT PLACE ANYTHING ON THEM.** `PLACE_VIEW_ON_SHEET` does that, and keeping them apart is what lets a register be built before the drawings exist. **VERSION 2 makes one sheet as well as many.** A number already used is refused whatever its capitals, naming the sheet that holds it; an empty number is refused; a sheet Revit will not create is said with Revit's own words, in `notCreated`. A title block may be named `Family: Type`, and a type name two families share is refused rather than guessed. Saying `none` makes sheets with no title block, flagged in `noTitleblock`. **VERSION 3 also makes copies of sheets handed in** (DUPLICATE_SHEETS merged in): each copy on its source's own title block, numbered as the source plus `numberSuffix`, named `namePrefix` plus the source's name, every number checked before anything is made. A placeholder or a sheet with no title block is not copied. **Neither job copies the views on a sheet** - the new sheets are empty; DUPLICATE_VIEWS and PLACE_VIEW_ON_SHEET do that. **VERSION 4 also makes new drawings from rows handed in as one value** (CREATE_SHEETS_FROM_TABLE merged in) - written by heron_sheet_list from the modeller's own file - in one call and one undo. The first row names the fields: Sheet Number is required, Sheet Name and Title Block optional, and each other field is filled into the new drawing's own parameter of that name, or else into its title block instance; never into a title block TYPE parameter. An empty field writes nothing, and a value Revit will not take is given back while its drawing is kept. For the rows and for numbers typed alike: each drawing is made in its own sub-transaction, and one whose number or name Revit refuses is taken back and given back with Revit's words; one number given twice makes neither; at most 1,000 in one call. previewOnly does the whole job and takes it back.

<a id="delete-revision"></a>

### Delete revision

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-18 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** delete that revision from the project.

Deletes one project revision - the Delete button of the revisions dialog - and only with `confirm` naming that revision: its element id, or Revit's own "Seq. N - description" - never a bare number, which a renumber moves. The caller passes it only after the owner has said yes for that revision. An issued revision is refused by name, and so is a delete that would renumber a later issued one. **DELETING ONE RENUMBERS EVERY LATER REVISION, AND THAT IS THE PART THAT CATCHES PEOPLE.** Delete revision 3 of 5 and the old 4 and 5 become 3 and 4. Every note, every email and every drawing that referred to "revision 4" now points at a different issue - and nothing in the model records that it moved. The numbers after the deletion are read back and reported for exactly that reason. **WHAT IT TOUCHED IS REPORTED**: the clouds that carried it, the sheets that showed it, what Revit deleted along with it, and every revision that was renumbered. When Revit refuses - the project's last revision, or one still in use - Revit's own reason is reported, never a guessed one. **ONE REVISION, HANDED IN BY A FIND** - by Revision Sequence, the number the dialog shows, or by description; two found is refused with both named. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16), so one undo puts the revision and its numbering back.

<a id="edit-revision"></a>

### Edit revision

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-17 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** change the revision description or date.

Changes one existing project revision - its description, date, issued to, issued by, show (cloud and tag, tag or none), numbering sequence, and the issued tick - every column of its row in Sheet Issues/Revisions. **ONE REVISION, HANDED IN BY A FIND.** Find it by Revision Sequence, the number the dialog shows, or by description; a find that brings back two is refused with both named, because descriptions repeat across a job - unless `confirmCount` says how many were found, and then every one changes in one call. **AN ISSUED REVISION IS LOCKED, AND THE REFUSAL NAMES IT.** Revit locks the description, date, issued to, issued by and numbering of an issued revision, so asking for any of them changes nothing and names the revision and the fields. `issueState=unissue` in the same call un-issues it first; show stays open, as it does in Revit. A numbering change that would renumber a later issued revision is refused the same way. **THE ISSUED TICK MOVES ONLY WHEN `issueState` SAYS SO** - "issue" after every other column, "unissue" before them. **EMPTY LEAVES A FIELD ALONE; <blank> WRITES AN EMPTY ONE.** **COMPARED FIRST, READ BACK AFTER.** A field already holding the value is named in `alreadyThat` and not written, so a repeat changes nothing and says so. A write that does not read back after another has gone in throws, and the whole call is rolled back. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="edit-revision-clouds"></a>

### Edit revision clouds

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-07 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** change the revision of these revision clouds to another revision, or delete the clouds.

Moves revision clouds from one revision to another - only the clouds handed in, so another sheet keeping the old revision is left alone - or deletes them. One call is one undo entry. **THE CLOUDS COME FROM A FIND OR THE SELECTION.** LIST_REVISION_CLOUDS finds them by sheet, view and revision; this changes exactly those. `fromRevision` is a guard: a handed cloud not on it is skipped and named. **WHAT THE SHEETS PRINT, BEFORE AND AFTER.** A cloud is what puts a revision on a sheet. Every sheet the clouds print on is read before and after, and `sheetEffect` names each revision that came onto or went off its revision block, and the sheet's current revision. **DELETE IS DESTRUCTIVE: `confirm` MUST BE THE COUNT.** Asked to delete, nothing goes unless `confirm` is the number of clouds that will go - the number the modeller was shown and agreed. Their tags go with them, named in `alsoDeleted`. **ALL OR NOTHING.** A cloud Revit will not move, or a delete that loses one, throws - and the whole call is rolled back rather than leaving half a set moved. Comments and Mark on clouds are WRITE_ELEMENT_PARAMETERS', handed the same clouds. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="edit-revision-numbering-sequence"></a>

### Edit revision numbering sequence

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-24 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** rename a revision numbering sequence or change its digits, start, prefix, suffix or custom list.

Changes one revision numbering sequence - the Edit button in Sheet Issues/Revisions > Customize Numbering, or Numbering Options on Revit 2020 and 2021: its name, and for a numeric sequence its minimum number of digits, starting number, prefix and suffix, or for an alphanumeric one its custom sequence, prefix and suffix. Empty leaves a field alone; <blank> writes an empty prefix or suffix. **THE CUSTOM SEQUENCE IS TAKEN WHOLE**, commas between the values; an empty or repeated value, or an ellipsis, is refused. **REVIT 2020 AND 2021 HAVE JUST TWO**, Numeric and Alphanumeric, with no rename and no minimum digits. **THE TYPE IS FIXED ONCE MADE**, so a value belonging to the other type is refused by name. **AN ISSUED REVISION KEEPS WHAT IT PRINTS** - a settings change is refused only when it would change what an issued revision prints on drawings already sent out, naming the revisions; one that leaves them as they are goes ahead and says so. A new name is allowed. A field already at the value asked is named in `alreadyThat` and not written; every write is read back, and a half-done edit is rolled back. <a id="export-sheets-to-pdf"></a>

### Export sheets to PDF

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-13 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** write these sheets out as PDF, and check the file is really there.

Exports sheets to PDF - one combined file or one per sheet - and reports the paths that ACTUALLY EXIST ON DISK afterwards, the same read-back EXPORT_VIEWS_TO_DWG uses and for the same reason. ASKING A PRINTER WAS DELIBERATELY NOT RE-AUTHORED, and that is the most important line here. The older way to reach a PDF is to drive a virtual printer through PrintManager. That route submits a real print job, and on a real office machine the installed printer list contains real physical copiers next to the PDF drivers. A wrong driver spends somebody else's paper on a shared device - an outward, unrecoverable side effect nobody asked for. So this fragment uses the export API and nothing else, and its declared release range is narrowed to the releases that carry it rather than widened by a printer fallback. A fragment that refuses an old release is honest; one that quietly prints on a copier is not. RISK IS **PUBLISH**. Nothing in the model changes. Files are written that get issued to other people, and one Ctrl+Z does not un-send a drawing. NO TRANSACTION, AND NONE IS NEEDED - export is document I/O, not a model edit.

<a id="find-sheets"></a>

### Find sheets

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-02 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** the sheets in this model, optionally narrowed by sheet number or by title.

Answers "which sheets" for everything that acts on sheets - renumbering, revisions, placing views, batch export to PDF or DWG. The sheet half of the spine FIND_VIEWS is the view half of (D-45). Matches on EITHER the sheet number or the sheet name, because both are what people say. "The M-series" is a number; "the ground floor sheets" is a name. A filter that only reads the number answers half the requests and returns a confident zero for the other half. PLACEHOLDER SHEETS ARE RETURNED, AND REPORTED SEPARATELY BY ID. A placeholder is a real sheet with a number and a name, carrying no titleblock, that cannot hold a view. The two things that act on sheets want opposite treatment: a renumbering or revision job MUST see them or it silently renumbers some of the set, while placing a viewport or exporting to PDF cannot use one at all. Silent omission is the worse failure of the two, so nothing is dropped here - the ids are handed over and the action decides. **"THE DRAWING LIST" IS AMBIGUOUS AND BOTH ANSWERS ARE RIGHT.** In Revit a sheet list IS a schedule, so that sentence can mean either the sheets themselves or the schedule that lists them: | What you meant | Use | |---|---| | The sheets — to place views on, renumber, export | **this fragment** | | The schedule that lists them — to add a column, export to CSV | `FIND_VIEWS`, viewType Schedule | `FIND_VIEWS` carries the same table, identically. An action that excludes them does so visibly; a filter that had already removed them would leave a renumbering job reporting success over an incomplete set, which is this repository's defining failure and the reason FIND_VIEWS counts what it skips. **VERSION 2 reads each sheet back as the drawing list.** One `findings` row per sheet - its number, its name and how many views are on it - with EMPTY on a sheet that holds none and PLACEHOLDER on one that cannot. A sheet VIEW TEMPLATE is not a sheet and is left out. Version 1's proof no longer describes the code and is kept as a record; the card is DRAFT until it is proved again. **VERSION 3 picks the sheets of an issue.** By one revision - its Seq., its description or its date - carried ANYWHERE on the sheet, not only as the latest; a description that fits two revisions is refused and both are named. And by a typed list of sheet numbers matched WHOLE: "179, 180" never picks 1790, where the part-match above would. Numbers that name no sheet, listed sheets without the revision and sheets Revit would not read are each said.

| **You get** | elements, placeholders, findings |

Lists the project's revision clouds - each one's revision (sequence, date, description), the view it is drawn in, the sheets it prints on, its Comments and Mark, and its tag - narrowed by sheet, by view and by revision. **A CLOUD IS DRAWN IN ONE VIEW AND PRINTS ON EVERY SHEET THAT VIEW IS ON.** Both are reported: the sheet is where it shows, the view is where to go to move it. **THIS IS WHY A REVISION CANNOT BE UNTICKED.** A sheet prints every revision a cloud on it carries, whatever its tick says. Narrowed to one sheet and one revision, this names the clouds that hold it there. **IT HANDS THE CLOUDS ON.** Its answer is the clouds themselves, so the next step acts on exactly what was listed - SET_SELECTION to select and zoom to them, EDIT_REVISION_CLOUDS to move them to another revision or delete them, WRITE_ELEMENT_PARAMETERS to set their Comments or Mark. **A FILTER THAT MATCHES NOTHING LISTS NOTHING**, and says which word missed - never every cloud in the project instead. Sheets or views handed in by the step before narrow a typed filter and never widen it.

<a id="list-revisions"></a>

### List revisions

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-07 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** every revision in the project and which sheets carry each one.

Lists the project's revisions in sequence, and for each one the sheets that show it. **The sheet list is the answer, not the revision list.** *"Which sheets go out with this issue"* is the question somebody is actually asking, and it decides what gets printed. A revision with no sheets against it is either not yet clouded or was clouded on a view that is on no sheet - both are worth finding before an issue rather than after. **A sheet shows a revision two different ways.** A cloud on it puts the revision there; so does ticking the revision on the sheet by hand, with no cloud anywhere. Revit reports both together and so does this - because both print, and a sheet that shows a revision is issued whichever way it got there. **And sheet by sheet (version 2).** Every sheet in register order with its revisions in sequence, the letter or number each PRINTS, whether each is ticked on the sheet, held by a cloud, or both, and its CURRENT revision - the last one. With `expectedLast` ("Seq. 21") the sheets that do not end on it come back in `lastDiffers`. `cloudOnly` names every revision that only a cloud keeps on a sheet - **which is why it cannot be unticked**; the clouds themselves are LIST_REVISION_CLOUDS'. **It also reads the Sheet Issues/Revisions dialog row by row**: each revision's numbering, date, description, issued tick, issued to, issued by and show setting, the number it actually prints on each sheet, the Per Project / Per Sheet setting, every numbering sequence with its settings, and the revision cloud arc length.

It is listed, marked EMPTY, and listed again in `emptySets`. **TWO SETS HOLDING EXACTLY THE SAME SHEETS AND VIEWS ARE FLAGGED.** Each is marked SAME with the other's name, and the pair is listed in `sameSets`. **THE IN-SESSION SET IS NOT COUNTED.** It lives only in the Revit session, not in the model, so a project with no other set answers none.

<a id="list-views-on-sheet"></a>

### List views on sheet

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-18 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** what is on each sheet and where - its viewports, legends and schedules, every sheet one view or legend is on, and any running off the sheet or overlapping another.

Answers what the sheets carry and where each thing sits on the paper - which viewports, legends and schedules one sheet holds, or every sheet one view or legend is on - each with its box corner to corner in millimetres, its viewport type, its view type and scale ("1 : 100") and its detail number. And it checks the layout: a box running off the sheet past its title block, and two viewports or schedules overlapping, each said with by how many millimetres. A question, read and never changed - it opens no transaction. **THE SHEET IS NAMED BY ITS NUMBER, OR "all" FOR EVERY SHEET**, matched whole and ignoring case. Left out, it is every sheet - so "does any view run off the sheet" needs no number. A number that matches no sheet is said by name and nothing is read; a blank one is refused rather than answered from the sheet in front or the first sheet in the list, which would be a confident answer about a sheet nobody asked about. To find a sheet by its title first, FIND_SHEETS takes part of a number or a title. **ONE VIEW BY NAME, ON EVERY SHEET IT IS ON.** A legend or a schedule can sit on many sheets. Named in `viewName`, whole and ignoring case, only its rows come back - one per sheet, with the box on each - and the sheets it is on are named. It is still measured against everything else on each of those sheets, so a legend overlapping a plan is found, but only a problem that involves it is said. A name on no sheet is said, with the names on the sheets that hold the text typed. Left out, it is every view. **OFF THE SHEET AND OVERLAPS, MEASURED ON THE BOXES.** The paper is the title block's extent on the sheet; a box past it is said side by side - left, right, bottom, top - with how far. Two boxes overlapping are said with how wide and how high the overlap is. Within half a millimetre is a layout snapped edge to edge, not a problem. A viewport's box is the view and its annotation, never the title under it. A sheet with no title block cannot be checked for running off, and is named as not checked rather than passed. **A SCHEDULE ON A SHEET IS NOT A VIEWPORT, SO IT IS GIVEN APART.** Revit shows a view on a sheet through a viewport and a schedule through a schedule instance, and the views Revit gives for a sheet leave the schedules out. Both are read here, and counted separately. A schedule split into pieces across the sheet is one schedule, named once with how many pieces. A revision schedule built into the title block belongs to the title block family, not to the sheet, and is counted apart rather than named. **LEGENDS ARE VIEWS ON THE SHEET**, shown through a viewport like a plan, so the legends on it come with the views and say Legend. A perspective 3D view has no scale and says so, rather than reporting a number Revit itself calls meaningless. **A PLACEHOLDER SHEET HOLDS NOTHING AND IS SAID TO BE ONE.** It is a number and a name with no title block, and it can hold no view. Among every sheet, placeholders are counted and left out. **A LONG ANSWER SAYS IT WAS CUT.** Each list stops before 60000 characters and its last row says how many were not written; the counts are never cut.

<a id="manage-sheet-sets"></a>

### Manage sheet sets

**DRAFT - not yet usable in a chat - refused until proved (D-117).**

**What it does:** save these sheets as a named set for printing.

Creates, renames or deletes the named sheet sets that appear in Revit's print and export dialogs - the saved lists an issue is printed from. **EVERY ROUTE GOES THROUGH THE PRINT MANAGER, AND THERE IS NO OTHER ONE.** A sheet set is an element, and it cannot be built with a constructor, renamed through its name, or removed with a delete. All three go through the print manager's sheet-set setting, which is an odd shape for a model change and is simply how Revit exposes it. **THE SETTING THROWS UNLESS THE PRINT RANGE IS SET FIRST.** Asking for it while the range is anything but "selected views" raises an error whose text is about the print dialog and says nothing about sheet sets. Every mode sets the range first. **THE PRINT MANAGER IS NOT TRANSACTIONAL.** The print range stays changed even if the surrounding transaction rolls back - it is application state, not document state - so it is read before it is set and put back afterwards, whatever happened in between, and the reply says which. **A SET IS A LIST OF VIEWS, AND A DELETED VIEW LEAVES A HOLE.** The set is written from the elements given, and what it holds afterwards is read back rather than assumed. Version 4 makes one set for each value of a sheet parameter, in one call - every sheet and view carrying that value goes into the set named for it, the value itself or with a prefix put in front. A set that already exists is left as it is and reported, unless bringing existing sets back in step was asked for. A parameter no sheet has is refused, naming it, and so is a value asked for that no sheet carries. Every mode writes a new set through the In-Session set, and the Print dialog's current set and In-Session selection are put back afterwards with the range. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

N - description". A bare yes, or a bare number, is refused and nothing changes. So is a merge that would renumber a later ISSUED revision. **BOTH MUST BE UNISSUED**, which is Revit's rule; the refusal names the issued one before Revit is asked. **ONE REVISION, HANDED IN BY A FIND** - by Revision Sequence or description. **READ BACK**: the merged revision must be gone and every cloud Revit moved must carry its new revision, or the whole merge is rolled back. The clouds moved, the sheets that showed it and the order before and after are handed back. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16), so one undo puts all of it back.

<a id="reorder-revision"></a>

### Reorder revision

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-18 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** move a revision up or down the project's revision sequence.

Moves one revision up or down the project's revision sequence - the Move Up and Move Down buttons in Sheet Issues/Revisions - one row at a time, or to the first or last place, and reads the order back. **MOVING A REVISION RENUMBERS IT AND EVERY REVISION IT PASSES**, issued ones included. So a move that would change the number of an ISSUED revision is refused, naming it: that number is printed on drawings already sent out. **ONE REVISION, HANDED IN BY A FIND** - by Revision Sequence, the number the dialog shows, or by description. Two found is refused with both named. The order before and after is handed back in full. A move that does not read back where it was asked is rolled back. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16), so one undo puts the order back.

<a id="report-sheet-title-blocks"></a>

### Report sheet title blocks

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-07 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** which title block is on each of these sheets, and which have none.

Says which title block family and type is on each sheet, and names the sheets that have none. IT EXISTS AS THE CALL TO MAKE BEFORE `SET_SHEET_TITLE_BLOCK`, because that fragment behaves in two entirely different ways depending on the answer. A target in the SAME family as what is already there is a safe swap; a different family means the old title block is deleted and everything held on it is lost. This is what tells you which of the two a drawing set is about to get - and on a real set it is usually both, because sheets accumulate borders from whichever template they were made in. **A SHEET WITH NO TITLE BLOCK IS A REAL FINDING, NOT A BLANK ROW.** It prints with nothing round the drawing, and it is invisible in the Project Browser - the sheet is there, numbered, and looks like all the others in the list. So those are counted and named rather than left as an empty cell for somebody to notice. **A SHEET WITH MORE THAN ONE TITLE BLOCK IS ALSO A FINDING**, and it is the one nobody looks for. Two borders stacked exactly on top of each other look like one, print like one, and mean a later swap changes whichever the API reaches first while the other stays. Reads only. It opens no transaction and changes nothing.

| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2024 |

<a id="set-print-settings"></a>

### Set print settings

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-08 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** set the paper size and orientation and save it as a print setting.

Sets the paper size, orientation and fit, and saves them as a named print setting - the middle link of the print chain: a sheet set to print, a setting to print it with, and the print itself. **THE PAPER SIZES COME FROM THE PRINT DRIVER, NOT FROM REVIT.** A size that exists on the PDF writer may not exist on the plotter in the corridor, and asking for one the current driver does not have fails in a way that reads as a Revit problem. What the driver actually offers is reported, so a refused size can be seen against the list rather than guessed at. **THE PRINT MANAGER IS NOT TRANSACTIONAL.** These settings are application state as much as document state: an undo does not reliably put the previous paper size back. That is worth knowing before treating this as a change like any other. **A NAME ALREADY IN USE IS REFUSED.** Saving over an existing setting is not what somebody means by "save this as A1 Landscape", and quietly replacing one another drawing set prints with is worse than the refusal. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16) - for the document side of it.

| **You get** | applied, saved as |

<a id="set-revision-settings"></a>

### Set revision settings

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-18 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** number revisions per project or per sheet, and set the revision cloud arc length.

Sets the two project-wide revision settings in Sheet Issues/Revisions: the Numbering switch - revisions numbered per project or per sheet - and the revision cloud arc length, in millimetres on paper. Empty leaves a setting alone. **SWITCHING THE NUMBERING RENUMBERS WHAT IS ALREADY PRINTED**, issued revisions included, so it is refused while any ISSUED revision shows on a sheet - each one named with its sheets. **THE ARC LENGTH IS CHECKED WITH REVIT FIRST** - whether it accepts the value - and read back within a tenth of a millimetre on paper, because Revit stores it on its own rounding grid; the value it stores is reported. A setting already at the value asked is named in `alreadyThat` and not written, so a repeat changes nothing. A write that does not read back after the other has gone in rolls both back. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="set-sheet-revisions"></a>

### Set sheet revisions

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-07 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** put that revision on these sheets, take it off, or swap it for another.

Attaches a revision to sheets, detaches it, or SWAPS it for another - the revision list that prints in a title block, without drawing a cloud. **REPLACE: "make today's revision the last one on these sheets instead of 28-Oct".** With `replaceWith` naming revision B, the revisions handed in are taken off and B is put on - only on the sheets that carried them, all in one undo entry. Every other revision on the sheet stays. **A SHEET CARRIES REVISIONS TWO WAYS AND THIS IS THE OTHER ONE.** A cloud on a sheet puts its revision in the schedule automatically. A revision can also be listed on a sheet with no cloud anywhere - which is how a whole-drawing issue is recorded - and that list is what this writes. **IT ADDS TO WHAT IS THERE, OR REMOVES FROM IT - IT NEVER OVERWRITES THE LIST.** A swap moves one revision for another and keeps the rest. Overwriting the list would silently drop every earlier issue off a title block, and nobody reads a revision block to check that last month's entries are still in it. **WRITING THIS LIST CAN MAKE REVIT PURGE AN UNUSED REVISION.** A revision on no sheet and in no cloud can vanish project-wide the next time sheet revisions are written. That is Revit's behaviour, not this fragment's, and it is why the revisions that still exist afterwards are read back and counted. **A CLOUD-DRIVEN REVISION CANNOT BE REMOVED THIS WAY - AND A REVISION CAN BE ON A SHEET BOTH WAYS AT ONCE.** After the write every sheet is read back for what it PRINTS. A sheet that still prints a revision taken off is named in `cloudDriven`, with the clouds that hold it in `cloudsHolding`, and is not counted as changed. Those clouds are moved to another revision, or deleted, by EDIT_REVISION_CLOUDS. A sheet the revision was never on is `notOnSheet`. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

| **You get** | sheets changed |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2024 |
| **Capability** | `SET_SHEET_REVISIONS` |

<a id="set-sheet-title-block"></a>

### Set sheet title block

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-28 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** put a different title block on these sheets.

Changes the title block on a set of sheets to one given type - the whole drawing set moved onto a new border in one call. IT EXISTS BECAUSE A TITLE BLOCK CHANGE IS A WHOLE-SET JOB DONE ONE SHEET AT A TIME. A client changes their border, or a project moves off the old one, and every sheet has to follow. The library could make sheets and list them and could not change what they are drawn on. **THERE ARE TWO DIFFERENT OPERATIONS HERE AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS SAFE.** If the new type is in the SAME family as what the sheet already has, the type is swapped on the existing instance and every instance-level value on it is kept. If it is a DIFFERENT family, the old title block is deleted and a new one placed - and anything typed into the old instance is gone with it. So the two are counted separately and the replaced sheets are named one by one, because *"48 sheets updated"* hides the four that quietly lost data. **WHAT SURVIVES A CROSS-FAMILY REPLACE, AND WHAT DOES NOT.** Sheet Number, Sheet Name, issue date and every other sheet parameter live on the SHEET, not on the title block, and are untouched either way. What is lost is anything held on the title block INSTANCE - a per-sheet override typed into the border, a moved revision schedule. That distinction is the one people get wrong, and it is why the replaced list is worth reading before the next step. **THE TYPE ARRIVES ALREADY FOUND.** The earlier library matched it inside the same call by a name substring, which picks silently and can pick wrong when two families carry the same type name. Finding the type is a filter's job in this library, and handing in a `FamilySymbol` makes the choice visible before anything is changed. **A TYPE THAT IS NOT A TITLE BLOCK IS REFUSED**, because Revit will place almost anything on a sheet and the result is a drawing with a door on it. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).
